thread:
devon (sales): Hey team — Starlit (prospect) wants to run a custom 13B variant for a search summarization POC. They asked about performance, compatibility with our KV cache, and a rough estimate of cost if they do a 2-week POC at ~50 qps sustained.
anya (solutions): Nice. Do we know if the model uses rotary embeddings or any nonstandard attention? that affects kernel selection and quantization options.
devon (sales): They uploaded the model metadata: says 'base = Llama-compat, rotary = true, seq_len=4096, fp16 weights, no fused-mlp'. Attaching their filename: model-starlit-13b-v1.safetensors (link).
praj (mlops): rotary + 4k context is fine, but the kv cache size will be larger. For 50 qps we need batching and prefix caching to hit latency targets. Are they OK with ~150ms p50?
devon (sales): Customer asked for <200ms p95 ideally. They said approximate average prompt length 120 tokens and response 60 tokens.
li (infra): For 50 qps sustained, assuming 120+60 tokens and 13B, with our optimized kernels and int8 quantization we can do ~60 qps per A100-80GB equiv node if we enable continuous batching and prefix caching. If they want 200ms p95 we'd need 2 nodes dedicated (or 1 node + burst). Need to validate variant quantization accuracy.
anya (solutions): Let's propose two options: (1) hosted POC with dedicated small pool (2 nodes) + enable kv prefix caching + int8 quantized variant — faster and cheaper than full fp16. (2) Dedicated trial with 1 node but higher SLA & burst credits. Pricing estimate ballpark?
devon (sales): They also asked about catalog onboarding time — can we have this model in the catalog and a quantized variant within 3 business days?
praj (mlops): If model weights are standard (safetensors) and repo-check passes, we can do an initial compatibility run in <24h, then quantization + eval in 48–72h. Need to run our eval prompts to check regression.
nia (security): Quick sec notes: verify no embedded proprietary tokenizer hacks, run license scan, and confirm they permit retention for eval. Also KMS — they require customer-managed keys (BYOK). We support KMS for Private and Dedicated, hosted needs additional review.
li (infra): BYOK is not available on our shared hosted pools today. For POC we can use isolated dedicated capacity (dedicated tenant) with KMS if sales signs off.
devon (sales): OK — will propose the dedicated POC. Need a simple deliverable list for the SOW. Can someone draft a short checklist?
anya (solutions): I'll draft: 1) catalog intake + compatibility tests 2) quantized variant build (int8) 3) perf run at 50 qps with caching 4) accuracy regression report (our eval harness) 5) KMS + network config 6) 2-week usage and cost estimate.
praj (mlops): Add: checkpoint of the quantization config we used (bitsandbytes + per-channel) and the exact eval prompt bundle.
 nia (security): Also add: license report + data retention policy + vulnerability quick-scan.
tom-deploy-bot: deploy request queued for infra-validation (request id: dv-1755000000) :gear:
li (infra): I'll validate infra sizing and KMS feasibility today. If infra thumbs-up, we can commit to the 3 business day onboarding timeline for the catalog variant.
devon (sales): Perfect. I'll send a proposal to Starlit this afternoon with the two options and the SOW bullet list. Thanks all. :pray:
anya (solutions): Ping me once they accept, will schedule a quick kick-off to collect eval prompts and test data.
li (infra): FYI — one risk: if the customer's model includes custom CUDA ops we'll have to fall back to fp16 and maybe degrade throughput. We'll flag that in the proposal.
devon (sales): Noted. I'll add a short risk section.
praj (mlops): final note — if they insist on deterministic sampling we need to enable seed sync and that reduces batching efficiency; call that out.
devon (sales): Great. closing thread — will update once I hear back.
